display.title: Episode 152: Torah, the Best Thing of All, Chapter 2
display.summary_short: Polishing our buttons for Moshiach, standing up when a parent enters, a whole family leads the Shema, and Rabbi Akiva shows the pirates the one treasure no one can steal.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens with simcha: when Moshiach comes, the small children who learn Torah will lead the great parade out of golus, so like soldiers before an inspection we must 'polish our buttons', our midos, with every mitzvah. After the Hakochainik march and the sponsor's message, Mitzvah Time continues the contest: a girl on the phone explains why honoring parents is written on the first tablet of the Ten Commandments, together with the mitzvos between a person and Hashem, and adds a Midrash of her own. The new mitzvah is to stand up when a parent enters the room, as the blind sage Rav Yosef did when he heard his mother's footsteps. A visiting family, winners of the Shofar Gadol contest, lead the Shema and thank their schools. The story concludes: pirates board Rabbi Akiva's ship and strip the merchants of everything, but Rabbi Akiva stays calm, because his treasure is the Torah he has learned. Afterwards the merchants apologize and ask him to become their teacher.
display.lesson: Torah is the one treasure no one can take away, and every mitzvah polishes us to greet Moshiach.
